nodes.description: The working model for SHILCA is that the duplication lowers nuclear NAD+ synthesis below what skeletal, cochlear and central nervous system tissue tolerate, not only below the retina's threshold as in LCA9. Nmnat1 knockout mice die in utero, which shows that some NMNAT1 activity is required outside the retina. The tissue-specific steps between NAD+ shortfall and chondrodysplasia, hearing loss or hypomyelination have not been studied.

nodes.description: An Alu-mediated tandem duplication spanning NMNAT1 exons 4 and 5 of the main isoform (c.299+526_*968dup) produces aberrant mRNAs and an approximately four-fold reduction in NMNAT1 expression in patient fibroblasts; some canonical transcript remains. In trans with the splice variant c.439+5G>T, total NMNAT1 mRNA in blood was about 25% lower than in controls and the isoform balance was disturbed. Because Nmnat1 knockout mice die as embryos and no human with biallelic null alleles is known, the duplication is interpreted as a strong but incomplete loss of function, more severe than the hypomorphs that cause retina-restricted LCA9.

nodes.description: The retinal component is the same process as in LCA9 (see Leber_Congenital_Amaurosis_9 for the PARP and SARM1 steps). Deleting Nmnat1 during retinal development in mouse causes early, severe photoreceptor loss through several cell death pathways. All SHILCA patients have congenital LCA; the compound heterozygous patient's electroretinogram was undetectable and her macular atrophy progressed.
